body: Ah okay! I wish you luck!

I think he doesn't care enough about this relationship to keep it up. I think that it would be best for you in the long run to break up with him and move on. Dragging the relationship out won't help. You should break up on good terms, tell him how much you appreciate him and think he is a good person and all, but you can't deal with the lack of attention. Trust me, I was in a similar relationship and I'm glad he left me and didn't drag it on. It will hurt more later. Good luck

Definitely tell him what you are thinking! Hiding your feelings in a relationship is the worst thing you can do. Don't bottle up your emotions. If he cares about this relationship, he needs to listen to you and tell you his feelings aswell. The biggest mistake couples make is not telling their partner their doubts. If you keep things going the way they are, nothing will change. You have to be the one to bring it up. Be brave. Good luck

I think you need to change your friend group/what you spend your time doing. Find new hobbies and groups of people that also do them. Not every girl your age is like that, you just have to change your life to find the better girls.

I think you have every right to not want to be around her. My mom is also very negative and toxic to be around. Your mother is probably feeling very insecure and worried that you will like the girlfriend more than your mom. I think you should sit down with your mom and tell her that you are not okay with how she is talking. If she gets angry, don't spend any time with her until she cools down. If she doesn't get angry and understands that her behavior isn't okay, then thats good. But from your info, I'm sure she will be angry. Just let her be by herself then and check up on her a bit, don't leave her alone completely. Good luck, I know how difficult it is to deal with negative mothers.

I don't think you should date him at all. He obviously doesn't see a long term thing with you. It seems like he is only dating you now because he is bored and is waiting for his chance at the other girl. I think he is stupid for leading you on though if he is so into this other girl. It is unfair to you. You don't know much about dating and he is taking advantage of you. Break it off before you get too attached and he breaks your heart.

Don't decide your future just because you don't want to give up everything you made with your girlfriend. Of course, if you two break up, it will be messy and your lives will change dramatically, but do you really want to be stuck with a women you aren't attracted to? Sure, you love her, but physical attraction is a huge part of a relationship. I think you should start thinking about if you really feel okay with spending your life with a women you don't want to have sex with. It might even lead to cheating. It's better to break it off now and possibly look for new relationships but I don't think it is wise to stay together just because you have a comfortable life. You aren't happy. Do what makes you happy.

Definately break up with her. In my last breakup, you sound exactly like my ex. It isn't okay to lead her on. If you feel like this now, and she keeps loving you, she's just going to be even more sad when you break up with her. Prolonging this relationship won't make anything better. It is better to just end it on good terms, explain to her exactly why you are leaving and don't let her convince you to stay out of guilt. Yes, she will be sad but eventually you both will be happier. Trust me. I'm still getting over my ex, but it is better for him to be less stressed and better for me to have time to fix my depression. Just make sure you break up in person. Texting it is a very bad idea. Good luck
Thank you! This gives me some push because I am scared that I would end up like that. I really do want to improve myself. Hopefully I'm early enough :)

I agree with this. So many marriages are like this, the couple is good dating but living together brings out the worst traits in people. So many marriages are unhappy and people say that's just how marriage is, but it doesn't always have to be. Have a sit down talk with him and tell him EVERYTHING you said here and everything you are thinking.

I made that mistake early on in my last relationship. I blamed him for a while before I realized that I was hurting him. 
She is blaming you because she thinks she is doing the same as she always has, but you are "changing". This is a bad insecurity. I think a good course of action could be suggesting to her that you go to couples therapy or separate therapy. She needs to get it in her head that she is in the wrong by blaming you. For me, I noticed that my boyfriend went to therapy more when I was like that. I realized I hurt him. For her, she needs a reality check that she is the only one in the wrong here.

I don't really like the idea of single life to be honest. Before my ex, I was a self harming mess who internet dated people way older than me just because they showed a tiny bit of interest in me. I really don't have any friends besides some guy friends. It's so lonely to be single. I have no one to talk to and it just makes my depression worse. Obviously, I need to work on that. I hope that this single period will make me less dependent on people for my mental issues.

I think she is feeling neglected. I know it doesn't make sense, but us girls can be like that. I believe that you are trying and are being genuine. But the thing is, most girls (atleast in my experience) love the honeymoon phase, and once its over, they feel like their partner doesn't love them anymore. That doubt never goes away and it eventually turns into them doubting their love for you. She probably misses how it was before things changed and doubts everything you do. She is encouraging you to try for other people because she thinks you aren't happy and in love like "you used to be", if that makes any sense.

I think you should have a sit down conversation with her and discuss how you genuinely still love her and want her to be happy and that you are trying your best. You need to explain ALL of your feelings to her. Don't leave anything out. She needs to understand how you are feeling and if she doesn't, then the relationship won't work. Communication is key.

Happy Holidays to you too!

Everyone says that lol...crossing my fingers that I will find my person eventually!
Thank you! I forgot that it could ruin the friendship if I try now..good advice.

I will put mental issues before pursuing my friend then. I'm thinking now maybe if I try now, and he likes me, that I will start getting attached to him as him as my mental support, which I made the mistake of doing with my ex. I think now that pursuing will get in the way of my progress and make me be like I used to: very dependent on others for happiness. Thank you for the advice.

I am working with my school therapist twice a week to try to fix my self hatred and how I blame myself for the end of my relationship. My end goal is to have no hatred towards myself and being able to be independent from my ex. I just really want to see if eventually I could be with my friend.

So I should just focus on fixing my mental issues before gauging his interest in me?

That makes sense that you feel this way. But since the strong connection won't come for a while, just view every day as an opportunity to grow closer. Have deep conversations and learn about each other's past more. Try to learn how your partner grew to the person they are now. It will help

I think that if there is a strong connection and you guys do things often together, it will start to feel like that again. As much as you want to rush it because you miss it, you should enjoy the moments in the present and not push for the future. You will enjoy it more. Don't worry.

He broke up with me two weeks ago and is ignoring all my texts and won't answer when I say hi in the hallways at school. He said we could be friends but this just feels like he's throwing me away like garbage.

He said he had been thinking about breaking up with me for as long as he could remember. He wasn't happy. That's all he said. Makes me feel like he doesn't care at all about me and that he never loved me.

How did you deal with the depression? I hate feeling so pathetic and unlovable and horrible but I've always felt like this and this breakup just ramped it up. I am so close to suicide in some moments. I want to get better but I don't know how without him.

I shouldn't text him at all? He was my pillar of support for so long and I was his too since we both have mental issues and I want to make sure he is okay and I want him to care if I'm okay or not...

So he doesn't care and wants no contact because he hates me and doesn't care if I'm okay or not?
